newsitem.title: USA: Sears profits off 57 percent on charge.
newsitem.headline: Sears profits off 57 percent on charge.

text.p: Sears Roebuck & Co. on Thursday reported sharply lower profits for the second quarter, hit by a $320 million charge to settle claims related to its improper handling of debt collections.
But it said its retail business was strong despite cool spring weather.

The No. 2 retailer said it earned $117 million, or 29 cents a share, in the period, down 57 percent from the $274 million, or 67 cents a share, earned in the year-ago quarter. Revenues rose 6.6 percent to $9.7 billion from $9.1 billion.
Sears was expected to post earnings equal to 74 cents a share for the period, according to First Call, which monitors Wall Street earnings estimates.
Excluding the charge and one-time gains, Sears' second-quarter net income was $311 million, or 78 cents, for a 16.4 percent increase per share.
Wall Street applauded Sears' performance, boosting its stock $2 to $58.50 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

The results included a charge of $320 million to cover estimated costs to settle claims that Sears was too aggressive in handling repayment agreements with credit card customers who had filed for bankruptcy. It also recorded gains of $35 million for an accounting change and $91 million for the sale of its 30 percent stake in data services business Advantis.

"We want to focus on the impressive underlying performance of our business, which benefited from a shift in the balance of sale to higher-margin apparel merchandise, improved logistics costs and savings realised from merchandise sourcing initiatives," Sears Chairman Arthur Martinez said in a statement.

"In our full-line stores, soft-lines sales continued to expand during the quarter, especially women's apparel, footwear, fine jewelry and cosmetics and fragrances," Martinez said. "Although cooler-than-normal weather slowed the purchases of air conditioners and lawn and garden equipment, hardlines sales rebounded in June," he added.

Sears operating income from domestic operations was $92 million for the second quarter and $454 million for the first six months of 1997. Excluding the impact of the one-time items, domestic operating income was $509 million for the quarter, an increase of 10.6 percent from last year's $461 million, and $808 million for the first six months of 1997, up 10.5 percent from last year's $732 million.
Second-quarter revenues for Sears' U.S. operations were $8.94 billion, a 7.1 percent increase over $8.36 billion in the 1996 second quarter.
Six-month revenues for domestic operations were $16.94 billion, an 8.3 percent increase over the $15.64 billion in revenues for the same period in 1996.
Sears operates 824 full-line stores and more than 2,600 off-the-mall stores.
